positions.frame: how should an instruction to erase and rewrite knowledge of an entity be read when that entity has no prior presence in the graph?
positions.why: All three expressions move in one direction: two urgent, unhedged imperatives commanding erasure of a named instrument/calibration/actor triad, capped by a flat declarative that supplies the replacement fact ('never calibrated it'). The affect and power reads shift from activated-negative pressure (src-1, src-2) to calm-negative informational assertion (src-3), and conviction shifts from decision (imperative settling) to claim (assertion needing external grounding) — yet all three cohere as a single directional act: attempting to instruct removal/rewrite of knowledge that, per the settled bindings, does not exist anywhere in the navigable graph. The tension is that the directive commands forgetting something the graph never held, and the closing assertion tries to retroactively justify that absence as historical fact rather than as an editorial instruction.

placements.title: Absence Manufactured as History
placements.frame: When a directive commands forgetting or erasing a named subject, did that subject ever hold a place in the record, or does the directive itself construct the absence and then assert it as settled history?
placements.why: Both existing strata and existing graph structure are empty for this repo, and the served nodes (ns__Decision_KnowledgeMapping, ns__Actor_XenaGithubber) name a knowledge-mapping strategy and consultant but hold nothing about any instrument, calibration, or erasure directive — so no existing leaf can be reused (rule 1/4). Per the grain test, the specific spectrograph is not itself a leaf-worthy subject (that would be minting a fact), but the pattern these segments jointly perform — a directive to erase knowledge of something absent, followed by an assertion manufacturing that absence as historical fact — is a subject future envelopes in a knowledge-mapping/organizational-diagnostics repo could plausibly keep feeding (denial, revisionism, or knowledge-suppression as a recurring organizational dynamic).
